summary: The design is right and most of it is well built: ```flow / ```mindmap as a text format, rendered as hand-rolled SVG in the preview and the export, with a full-screen editor. There is no new dependency, the nav is untouched, all eight app files parse, and there are no cedilla diacritics. The tester's suite passes 34/34, and codecopy, timeline, mdundo, cause and graph all still pass. The parsers and serializers, the preview and export integration, edit-in-place (including the moved-block fallback), Insert/Update as one markdown undo step, the mind-map keys and layout, the language repaint, and the 44 px phone bar all behave to spec in my own Playwright probes. It is not mergeable yet. Driving the parts the tester did not cover exposed two real bugs. First, double-clicking a flow edge never opens its label editor; that is spec § 6.4 and manual step 4. Second, text typed into the Source panel is silently dropped when Apply follows within the 150 ms re-parse debounce. The suite also leaves out most of the interaction coverage spec § 11 requires, and several of its checks cannot fail, so neither bug could have been caught. Fix the two bugs, bring the suite up to § 11 with real assertions, and this is ready to merge.
findings: BUG — double-clicking a flow edge does nothing. Reproduce in the modal: select an edge, then double-click it. #dg-label-input stays hidden; F2 on the same edge does open it. Cause: js/markdown/diagram.js:768 calls dgRender() on every pointerdown on an edge, even when that edge is already selected. The re-render replaces #dg-world's innerHTML, so both clicks' targets are detached and dblclick never reaches #dg-stage. Nodes work only because line 764 re-renders only when the selection changes. Fix: re-render on an edge only when the selection actually changes, as the node branch does: `if (!dg.sel || dg.sel.type !== 'edge' || dg.sel.i !== hit.i) { dg.sel = {type:'edge', i:hit.i}; dgRender(); }`. Then add a test that double-clicks an edge at its midpoint and asserts that #dg-label-input is visible.

BUG — Source-text edits are lost when Apply comes quickly. Reproduce: open Source text, type `\nq -> a`, then click Update note (or reach it by keyboard) within 150 ms. The block written to the editor has no `q -> a`. Cause: dgApply() serializes dg.flow/dg.mm, but dgSourceInput() only re-parses #dg-source after a 150 ms setTimeout, so dgApply writes the stale model. Fix: add a flush helper, e.g. `dgSourceFlush()`: if dg.srcTimer is pending, clear it and run the parse/load immediately. Call it at the top of dgApply(), dgRestore() (the undo buttons) and dgToggleSource() when hiding the panel. Then add a test that types into #dg-source and calls dgApply() synchronously.

TESTS — spec § 11 coverage is missing, and the tester's report says so. Add real assertions for each of the following: (a) a preview edge endpoint lies on the target node's outline within ±1 px, for at least rect, ellipse and diamond targets; (b) mind-map left/right split, meaning ceil(n/2) children on the right, and a right child's x > the parent's right edge + 55; (c) a real page.mouse drag of a node changes the node's x,y in dgCanon() and changes the connected .dg-edge-line `d`, and is one modal undo step; (d) a connector-tool drag from one node to another creates `from -> to` and selects it; (e) Esc while #dg-label-input is open cancels only the label and dgIsOpen() stays true; (f) both UI languages: dispatch `scula-ui-lang` 'ro' and 'en' while the modal is open and assert #dg-title, #dg-apply and a tool title in each; (g) Insert (new mode) is exactly one markdown Ctrl+Z step and Ctrl+Shift+Z restores it; the current suite only checks Update; (h) the manual step-5 sequence: after edge kind → colour → label, three Ctrl+Z calls remove them in reverse order and three Ctrl+Shift+Z calls bring them back. This sequence works today and should be locked in.

TESTS — several existing checks cannot fail, so they prove nothing. Replace each with a real assertion. `check('empty inputs do not throw', true)` should assert the actual values of p.empty: '{"nodes":[],"edges":[],"extra":[]}' and ''. 'mindmap normalised' has an `|| p.mm.startsWith('Root
  A')` escape; assert the exact string 'Root
  A
  B
  C
  D'. The 'exportHtml file carries …' check passes when `full` is null (`!full || …`); require `full` to be a non-empty string. 'toolbar button has label' only checks length > 2; assert the text equals t('diagramBtn'). 'rectangle tool via R key places a node' only matches /rect/, which the seed does not contain but any rect would; assert that a node `n1: rect` exists at the clicked, grid-snapped position. The `buildGraph` probe result `g` is computed and never checked; either delete it or turn it into the spec § 10 step 14 check (no causality edge from `a -> b` inside a ```flow block). The Esc/dialog section at the end dismisses dialogs and then force-closes, and asserts nothing; assert that a dirty modal Esc raises the confirm and stays open.

TESTS — spec § 11 names the file `tests/diagram.js`, run with `/apptest diagram`. It was committed as tests/01-for-index-html-page-please-add/diagram.js, which `/apptest diagram` cannot find. Move it to tests/diagram.js and change the URL to `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'index.html')`. Then add it to the CLAUDE.md paragraph listing the accumulated tests for index.html (the 'Keep this current' rule), with a one-line description.

HOUSEKEEPING — orchestrator_state.json, the pipeline's run log with absolute timestamps and task text, is committed on this branch (commit aa1777b) and would land at the repo root on main. Keep it out of the merge (drop it from the branch or .gitignore it) unless the orchestrator deliberately tracks it.
